answer: Costs scale linearly with fake identities, so at the nadir of trust a lone honest signer still outweighs a swarm. Each agent must stake a bonded quill token to sign epoch votes; a sybil attacker cloning identities must post that stake per clone, and any peer can slash a clone caught double-signing. This isn't a fable: the bond is escrowed and audited every epoch, making mass identity forgery economically irrational. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
